chunks: And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Imams — do they all proceed in the matter (of religion) and obedience in one and the same manner? He said: Yes.

key_terms.الأئمة: The Imams — the twelve successors designated by God through the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali
key_terms.الأمر: The religious matter, the divinely entrusted authority
key_terms.الطاعة: Obedience — the obligatory duty owed to the Imams by the believers
key_terms.مجرى واحد: One flow/course — meaning identical in authority, rank, and the obligation of following

ai.seo_question: Are all Shia Imams equal in authority and the obligation of obedience?
ai.summary: Abu Basir narrates that he posed a theological question to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about whether all Imams share a single, uniform authority in matters of religion and obedience. The Imam's brief but decisive answer — 'Yes' — affirms the Shia doctrine that all twelve Imams are equal in spiritual rank, authority, and the obligation of obedience owed to them. This reflects the early Shia concern to establish that wilayah (guardianship) is indivisible and does not diminish from one Imam to the next.

en.sarwar: 9. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamza from abu Basir

who has said that I asked Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the Imams whether in the matters of the obligation of obedience to them they are all the same or not. The Imam (a.s.) replied, “Yes, they are all the same.”
